In Fall 2020 I taught a semester-long discrete math course at UWO for second-year computer
science undergraduates. The course was *fully asynchronous*, which forced a number of innovations.

I curated a textbook on zyBooks and recorded a series of
[videos on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLXAOfwfSuiKm3cL-JftD9ndrjYi7fPcqN) to
accompany the text, and ran an active discussion forum on Piazza. With a lot of help from my
department we wrote hundreds of WeBWorK questions, which were then used on the exams.

I gave a talk about the course design at a conference on E-Assessment in Mathematical Sciences.
This has been the most challenging and the most rewarding course I have ever taught.
